the development of an automatic classification of the geological model using photogrammetric techniques, which will be used as input to a machine learning model to automatically classify lithologies and contact zones on the mining front.
the automation of the lithological mapping in open pit mines, using UAVs and photogrammetry to acquire the data, and the use of machine learning to automatically classify the geological model.

the automated geological mapping on mining front using UAVs is a feasible and cost-effective solution for the mining industry.

the use of UAVs and machine learning techniques to automate the geological mapping of open pit mining fronts is a reality, and that the accuracy of the automated classification can reach 90% when compared to the manually classified models.
the UAVs are a valuable tool to assist the mine planner and geologist in the geological mapping and modelling process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is possible to use UAVs to automatically classify the geological model of a mine face, using the point cloud as a base for machine learning techniques, and that the accuracy can be above 90% for the lithological classes, and above 95% for the contact zones.
the use of UAV for automated geological mapping of mining front is feasible, but it requires a lot of work and a lot of data to be trained.

the automated classification of the lithologies using machine learning techniques, when applied to UAV photogrammetry point clouds, presents a good accuracy when compared to the traditional methods, and it can be a valuable tool to the mine planning team, as it can be used to generate a 3D geological model of the open pit mining face, which can be updated daily, and used to improve the planning of the mining operations.
